reconcile: 440 g of bed powder at 1.5 g/cm3 is 293 cm3: a 12.9 mm layer of the 170 mm cylinder, i.e. a short build (or a smaller cylinder), where chapter 3's 30 mm build in the full cylinder takes about 1 kg. Both are the bed alone; the supply's excess is on top.
caveats: k7m2q9 is 630 bronze. Al atomizes coarser at the same 40 kHz (the capillary wavelength goes as (surface tension / density)^(1/3), about 1.3x for Al against Cu alloys), so its share under 63 um is an upper estimate for Al. The lab's Al 4047 powders looked coarse under the SEM (DAL #159).

The 63-250 um and >250 um powder can be remelted in a later run (more oxygen each time), so little metal is lost; it doesn't cut the number of runs, since each run still makes the same share of fines.

A cup charge is limited by the cups, not the crucible: four 2.5 in cups hold 59 cm3 of metal, a quarter of the 225. The Oct 27 rod pieces were about 125 mm long (270 g each of 3/4 in rod), so cups that long would about double the charge.
